experiences.name: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel
experiences.description: Explore one of the world's greatest art collections, culminating in Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling. Book skip-the-line tickets in advance to maximize your time among thousands of masterpieces spanning centuries of artistic achievement.

experiences.name: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk
experiences.description: Wander through the cobblestone streets of Trastevere sampling supplì (fried rice balls), artichokes alla romana, fresh pasta, and local Frascati wine at family-run trattorias and street food stalls. This bohemian neighborhood offers Rome's most authentic culinary atmosphere after dark.

experiences.name: Borghese Gallery Art Experience
experiences.description: Discover Bernini's stunning sculptures and Caravaggio's dramatic paintings in this intimate baroque villa. Entry is strictly timed and limited to 360 visitors, creating an exclusive and unhurried art experience unlike any other museum in Rome. Reservations are mandatory.

experiences.name: Campo de' Fiori Market & Cooking Class
experiences.description: Start your morning selecting fresh seasonal ingredients at the vibrant Campo de' Fiori market, then join a hands-on cooking class where a local chef teaches you to make homemade pasta, cacio e pepe, and tiramisu. You'll leave with recipes and memories to last a lifetime.

experiences.name: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Sunset Tour
experiences.description: Walk through the ancient heart of the Roman Empire at golden hour when crowds thin and the light turns magical. A guided tour of the Forum and Palatine Hill brings history to life through art, architecture, and storytelling, revealing frescoes, mosaics, and imperial ruins in stunning detail.
experiences.location: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum, historic center

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Rome
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Rome airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Use this time to rest on the flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, take the Leonardo Express train from Fiumicino Airport to Roma Termini (approx. €14, 32 minutes). Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and freshen up. Take a relaxed orientation walk around your neighborhood to get your bearings — find the nearest supermarket, metro stop, and local piazzas.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll to the nearby Piazza Navona (free entry) to soak in the baroque atmosphere, street artists, and the iconic Fountain of the Four Rivers. Enjoy the lively early evening crowd as the golden hour light hits the cobblestones.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick coffee and cornetto (€1.50–€2.50) at a bar near the hotel upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick slice of pizza al taglio near Roma Termini for €2–€4 per slice — fast, authentic, and budget-friendly.
meals.dinner: Trattoria da Tonino near Piazza Navona — a classic no-frills Roman trattoria with pasta dishes from €8–€12. Try cacio e pepe or carbonara.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a 48-hour or 72-hour public transport pass (€7/€12) at Termini — it covers buses, trams, and metro and will save money over single tickets throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Vatican Museums and Sistine Chapel — book tickets online in advance to skip the line (€20 standard entry). Arrive early (9:00 AM) to beat the crowds. Spend 2–3 hours exploring the galleries, the Gallery of Maps, and Michelangelo's breathtaking Sistine Chapel ceiling.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk across to St. Peter's Basilica (free entry — no ticket needed for the church itself). Climb to the top of the dome for panoramic views of Rome (€8 on foot, €10 by elevator). Afterwards, cross the Tiber and walk along the river toward Castel Sant'Angelo for exterior photos.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the charming Trastevere neighborhood on foot — winding cobblestone streets, ivy-covered buildings, and a vibrant local atmosphere. Browse the piazzas and pop into the beautiful Santa Maria in Trastevere basilica (free).

meals.breakfast: Bar San Calisto in Trastevere or a local bar near the hotel — espresso and cornetto for under €2.50.
meals.lunch: Forno Roscioli near Campo de' Fiori — grab fresh-baked pizza bianca or a suppli (fried rice ball) for €3–€5. Eat standing or find a bench.
meals.dinner: Da Enzo al 29 in Trastevere — beloved local trattoria, pasta from €9–€13. Arrive early or expect a short wait. Cash preferred.

day_by_day.notes: Dress code for the Vatican: no bare shoulders or knees. Bring a scarf or light layer. The Vatican is very walkable from the Trastevere area.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Colosseum, Roman Forum, and Palatine Hill — a combined ticket costs €16 and covers all three sites. Book online to avoid queues. Spend the morning walking through 2,000 years of history. The Roman Forum and Palatine Hill alone can take 1.5–2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk uphill to Capitoline Hill (Campidoglio) for free — enjoy the Piazza del Campidoglio designed by Michelangelo and the sweeping views over the Roman Forum. Visit the Capitoline Museums (€15) — one of the world's oldest public museums, housing the original Marcus Aurelius statue and stunning ancient sculptures.
day_by_day.evening: Walk to the Circus Maximus (free, outdoor) and through the Aventine Hill neighborhood. Find the famous Knights of Malta Keyhole on Piazza dei Cavalieri di Malta — peek through for a perfectly framed view of St. Peter's dome. Free and magical at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Caffè Propaganda near the Colosseum area — or grab a pastry and espresso at any local bar for €2–€3.
meals.lunch: Arco di Costantino food trucks or nearby sandwich shops (panino) around the Colosseum area — budget €5–€8. Avoid sit-down restaurants near tourist sites as they inflate prices.
meals.dinner: Pizzarium Bonci in Prati neighborhood (a short bus ride) — world-famous pizza al taglio by master baker Gabriele Bonci. Sold by weight, budget €8–€12 for a satisfying meal.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes — today involves a LOT of walking on uneven ancient stone surfaces. Bring water; Rome has hundreds of free drinking fountains called 'nasoni' throughout the city.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Borghese Gallery — one of Rome's finest art museums housing Bernini sculptures and Caravaggio paintings. Tickets must be booked in advance (€15, timed entry). Afterward, take a free stroll through the beautiful Villa Borghese gardens — Rome's version of Central Park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down the Spanish Steps (free) and explore the upscale Via Condotti area — window shopping is free! Head to the Trevi Fountain (free) — toss a coin and make a wish. Then walk to the Pantheon (€5 entry since 2023) — a nearly perfectly preserved ancient Roman temple, now a church. Marvel at the 2,000-year-old oculus.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the Campo de' Fiori market square (evening atmosphere, vendors pack up by afternoon but the piazza stays lively). Explore the nearby Jewish Ghetto neighborhood — beautiful, historic, and less touristy.

meals.breakfast: Antico Caffè Greco near the Spanish Steps (splurge option, €5–€8) or a neighborhood bar for the usual €2–€3 espresso and pastry.
meals.lunch: Mercato di Campo de' Fiori area — grab street food or a sandwich from a local alimentari (deli). Budget €5–€8.
meals.dinner: Osteria dell'Ingegno near the Pantheon — hearty Roman pasta and antipasti. Look for the fixed-price lunch/dinner menu (menù del giorno) at €12–€15 including primo, secondo, and water.

day_by_day.notes: The Borghese Gallery limits visitors strictly — latecomers may be turned away. Arrive 10 minutes early. The gallery visit is exactly 2 hours.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning food tour of the Testaccio neighborhood — Rome's historic working-class district and the true heart of Roman food culture. Visit the Testaccio Market (Mercato di Testaccio) — a covered local market with fresh produce, cheese, cured meats, and street food stalls. Try suppli, artichokes, and local cheeses for €1–€3 each.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the non-Catholic Cemetery (Cimitero Acattolico) in Testaccio — a hauntingly beautiful and free (donation suggested) cemetery where Keats and Shelley are buried. Nearby, see the Pyramid of Cestius (exterior free) — a genuine Egyptian-style pyramid built in 12 BC, one of Rome's most unexpected sights.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Pigneto neighborhood — a hip, artsy, local district beloved by young Romans and artists. Explore street art, independent boutiques, and enjoy Rome's aperitivo culture: many bars offer free snacks with a drink (€5–€8 per drink).

meals.breakfast: Grab a fresh cornetto and cappuccino at the Testaccio Market for €2–€3.
meals.lunch: Eat at the Testaccio Market food stalls — a full and satisfying lunch of Roman street food for €8–€12. Try the trapizzino (stuffed pizza pocket) and a glass of local wine.
meals.dinner: Remo a Testaccio — a legendary no-frills Roman pizzeria, cash only, pizza from €7–€10. Locals line up for it. Arrive before 8 PM to avoid a long wait.

day_by_day.notes: Testaccio is considered the birthplace of Roman cuisine — this is the best day for serious food lovers. The market is open Monday–Saturday, mornings only (closes around 2 PM).

day_by_day.morning: Day trip option: Take the train to Ostia Antica (€1.50 on a standard transit ticket from Roma Porta San Paolo station) — Rome's ancient harbor city, far less visited than Pompeii but equally impressive. Wander through ancient streets, mosaics, theaters, and baths for €12 entry. Easily 3–4 hours of exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Rome by early afternoon. Visit the Palazzo Doria Pamphilj on Via del Corso — a stunning private palace-turned-gallery with works by Velázquez, Caravaggio, and Raphael. Entry €16 and often uncrowded. The audio guide narrated by the current Prince Doria Pamphilj is charming and included.
day_by_day.evening: Spend the evening revisiting your favorite piazzas — Piazza Navona, Piazza della Rotonda (near the Pantheon), or Piazza del Popolo. Enjoy a gelato (€2–€3 at a non-tourist gelateria — look for natural colors, not neon) and people-watch as Romans enjoy their evening passeggiata.

meals.breakfast: Pack a picnic breakfast from a nearby supermarket (Conad or Carrefour) — yogurt, fruit, and pastry for under €4. Eat on the train to Ostia.
meals.lunch: Bring a packed lunch or grab food at the Ostia Antica café — budget €6–€10. Alternatively, there's a small bar inside the archaeological park.
meals.dinner: Enoteca Corsi near the Pantheon — a historic wine bar and trattoria open since 1937. Daily handwritten menu of Roman classics, pasta from €9–€11. Very local, very authentic.

day_by_day.notes: Ostia Antica is one of Rome's most underrated gems — far less crowded than the Roman Forum and equally atmospheric. Wear sunscreen and a hat as the site is largely open-air.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — revisit any missed sights or simply wander. Consider the free Basilica di Santa Maria Maggiore (one of Rome's four major basilicas) or the Basilica di San Giovanni in Laterano (€5 for the cloister). Both are stunning and often overlooked by tourists focused on the Vatican.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping at Campo de' Fiori or the area around the Pantheon. For budget souvenirs, skip tourist shops and head to the Porta Portese flea market (Sundays only) or look for local artisan stalls. Pick up vacuum-packed pasta, local coffee, or a small ceramic piece as gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — treat yourself to a slightly nicer sit-down meal to celebrate the trip. Ristorante Armando al Pantheon (book ahead) or Osteria Barberini — classic Roman pasta and secondi in a warm, unhurried setting. Budget €20–€28 per person for a full meal with wine.

meals.breakfast: One last proper Italian bar breakfast — espresso and a warm cornetto alla crema. Savor it. Budget €2.50.
meals.lunch: Light lunch — a fresh panino from an alimentari or a slice of pizza al taglio. Budget €4–€6. Keep it light before the farewell dinner.
meals.dinner: Farewell splurge dinner — Armando al Pantheon or similar. Antipasto, pasta, dessert, and a carafe of house wine for €22–€30 per person. Well worth it as a final Roman memory.

day_by_day.notes: Check your flight departure time and plan transport accordingly — the Leonardo Express from Roma Termini to Fiumicino takes 32 minutes and runs every 30 minutes. Budget at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for the journey and check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & Check-In: Flight lands at 13:00, so use the morning slot for transit. Take the Leonardo Express train from Fiumicino Airport to Roma Termini (30 min, ~€14), then taxi or bus to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented with a neighborhood stroll around your beachfront area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle Neighborhood Exploration: Since arrival is at 13:00 and check-in takes time, spend the afternoon leisurely exploring the area near the resort. Walk along the waterfront promenade, visit a nearby piazza, and pick up a local map. Head toward central Rome if energy allows — wander the Prati neighborhood near Castel Sant'Angelo for a relaxed introduction to the city.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk: Join the guided evening walk through Trastevere's cobblestone streets. Sample supplì (fried rice balls), Roman-style artichokes, and local wines at various stops. A perfect low-key introduction to Roman food culture after a travel day.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a quick espresso and cornetto at the airport café upon landing
meals.lunch: Light bite near the resort or at Roma Termini — try a slice of pizza al taglio from a local bakery (~€4–6)
meals.dinner: Included in the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk; supplement with a glass of house wine at a Trastevere osteria if still hungry (~€8–12)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Pre-book the Trastevere evening walk in advance as spots fill quickly. Validate all public transit tickets before boarding. The Trastevere walk typically starts around 18:30–19:00, which aligns perfectly with your arrival schedule.

day_by_day.morning: Vatican Museums & Sistine Chapel: Start early with a pre-booked timed entry (doors open 09:00) to beat the crowds. Spend 2.5–3 hours exploring the Gallery of Maps, Raphael Rooms, and culminating in Michelangelo's awe-inspiring Sistine Chapel ceiling. Book skip-the-line tickets online in advance (~€20–27).
day_by_day.afternoon: St. Peter's Basilica & Square: Directly adjacent to the Museums, entry to St. Peter's Basilica is free. Climb the dome for panoramic views of Rome (~€8 with elevator, ~€6 on foot). Afterward, relax in St. Peter's Square and soak in Bernini's magnificent colonnade.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Prati neighborhood: The upscale-casual Prati district near the Vatican is perfect for a mid-range dinner. Explore the streets around Via Cola di Rienzo for authentic Roman trattorias.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café — cappuccino and cornetto is the classic Roman start (~€2–4)
meals.lunch: Quick lunch at a Prati deli or sandwich shop near the Vatican — try a tramezzino or supplì (~€8–12)
meals.dinner: Trattoria Der Pallaro or similar in Prati — cacio e pepe, saltimbocca alla romana, and house wine (~€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Vatican Museums MUST be pre-booked — walk-up queues can be 2–3 hours long. Dress code required for St. Peter's: covered shoulders and knees. Arrive at the Museums by 09:00 sharp. Consider a guided tour for deeper context on the art collection (~€35–50 with guide included).

day_by_day.morning: Campo de' Fiori Market & Cooking Class: Start at 09:00 at the vibrant open-air market selecting fresh seasonal produce, cheeses, and herbs with a local chef. Then head to a nearby kitchen for a hands-on cooking class learning to make pasta, bruschetta, and a classic Roman secondo. Classes typically run 09:00–13:00 (~€65–85 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Jewish Ghetto & Largo Argentina: After the cooking class, walk off your feast exploring the historic Jewish Ghetto. Visit the Portico d'Ottavia ruins and peek into the ancient Roman cat sanctuary at Largo Argentina (free). Browse local artisan shops and boutiques in this charming quarter.
day_by_day.evening: Aperitivo Hour & Dinner in the Centro Storico: Join the Roman aperitivo tradition at a bar near Piazza Navona (spritz or Negroni with free snacks, ~€8–10). Then enjoy dinner at a trattoria near Piazza Navona or Campo de' Fiori.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before the market — espresso and pastry at a local café near Campo de' Fiori (~€3–5)
meals.lunch: Eat what you cooked in the cooking class! A full Roman meal prepared by your own hands
meals.dinner: Osteria del Pegno or similar near Piazza Navona — Roman classics like rigatoni all'amatriciana and tiramisù (~€28–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Campo de' Fiori market runs Monday–Saturday mornings, closing around 13:00 — timing aligns perfectly with the cooking class. Book the cooking class at least a week in advance. The Jewish Ghetto area is very walkable and compact. Wednesday evenings in Rome are lively but not overwhelmingly crowded.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Experience: Pre-booked timed entry is mandatory (entry every 2 hours, max 360 visitors). Arrive for the 09:00 slot to explore Bernini's breathtaking sculptures — Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina — and Caravaggio's dramatic canvases in this intimate baroque villa. (~€15 entry + €2 booking fee).
day_by_day.afternoon: Villa Borghese Gardens & Pincian Hill: After the gallery, stroll through the beautiful Villa Borghese park. Rent a rowboat on the lake (~€5/30 min), visit the Pincian Hill terrace for sweeping views over Piazza del Popolo and Rome's rooftops, and relax under the umbrella pines.
day_by_day.evening: Spanish Steps & Tridente Neighborhood: Walk down to the Spanish Steps at golden hour for beautiful light. Explore the chic Via Condotti area window shopping, then head to the Tridente neighborhood for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a café near the resort before heading out
meals.lunch: Picnic in Villa Borghese Gardens — buy fresh bread, prosciutto, cheese, and fruit from a nearby alimentari (~€10–15)
meals.dinner: Il Sorpasso or Osteria dell'Angelo near the Tridente — hearty Roman cuisine with excellent local wines (~€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets MUST be reserved in advance — they sell out days or weeks ahead. The gallery only allows 2-hour visits, so plan accordingly. Bring sunscreen and water for the afternoon park stroll as June can be warm. The Pincian Hill terrace is free and one of Rome's best viewpoints.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Morning Visit: Beat the heat and crowds with an early 09:00 visit to the Roman Forum and Palatine Hill. Stroll through the ancient heart of the empire — the Via Sacra, Temple of Saturn, and the imperial palaces on Palatine Hill. Combined ticket with Colosseum (~€16–18, pre-book online).
day_by_day.afternoon: Colosseum Visit: Use your combined ticket to enter the iconic Colosseum (included in the morning ticket). Explore the arena floor and underground hypogeum if booked. Afterward, cool down with a gelato near the Colosseo metro stop — try Fatamorgana or a trusted gelateria (look for 'artigianale' signs).
day_by_day.evening: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Sunset Tour: Return for the magical golden-hour experience as the sun sets over the ancient ruins. The light transforms the Forum into something otherworldly and crowds thin considerably. This is the perfect evening activity — either self-guided with your existing ticket or join a guided sunset tour (~€25–40 with guide).

meals.breakfast: Café near the hotel — classic Roman breakfast of espresso and cornetto (~€3–5)
meals.lunch: Testaccio neighborhood lunch — one of Rome's most authentic food districts. Try Flavio al Velavevodetto for Roman offal classics or Da Remo for pizza (~€15–22 per person)
meals.dinner: Testaccio Market area dinner — Osteria Degli Amici or similar for a relaxed, local Friday evening meal (~€25–32 per person)

day_by_day.notes: June heat in Rome can be intense — start the Forum early (09:00) before temperatures peak. Bring a refillable water bottle; Rome's 'nasoni' street fountains offer free cold drinking water throughout the city. The sunset tour/visit pairs beautifully with the morning visit as you see the ruins in completely different light. Friday evenings in Testaccio are wonderfully local and festive.

day_by_day.morning: Piazza Navona & Pantheon District: Explore Piazza Navona (Bernini's Fountain of the Four Rivers) early before the crowds arrive. Walk to the magnificent Pantheon — one of the best-preserved ancient buildings in the world. Entry now requires a ticket (~€5). Admire the oculus and marvel at 2,000-year-old engineering.
day_by_day.afternoon: Trastevere Afternoon Wander: Cross the Tiber to explore Trastevere in daylight — visit the stunning Basilica di Santa Maria in Trastevere (free), browse artisan shops, and discover hidden piazzas. This medieval neighborhood is Rome at its most romantic and photogenic.
day_by_day.evening: Gianicolo Hill Sunset & Farewell Dinner: Climb to the Gianicolo (Janiculum) Hill for the best panoramic view of Rome at sunset — completely free and spectacular. Then descend for a special farewell dinner in Trastevere at a mid-range restaurant with outdoor seating.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Sant'Eustachio il Caffè near the Pantheon — arguably Rome's best coffee (~€3–6)
meals.lunch: Lunch in Trastevere — Da Enzo al 29 or Tonnarello for authentic Roman pasta and pizza (~€18–25 per person)
meals.dinner: Grazia & Graziella or Osteria der Belli in Trastevere — romantic outdoor dinner with Roman specialties and local wine (~€30–40 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday is Rome's busiest day for tourists — arrive at Piazza Navona and the Pantheon by 09:00–09:30 for the best experience. The Pantheon now requires timed entry tickets purchased online. Trastevere on Saturday afternoon is lively and fun. The Gianicolo sunset view is free and often overlooked by tourists — a real hidden gem. Book dinner reservations in advance for Saturday evening.

day_by_day.morning: Castel Sant'Angelo & Tiber Walk: Visit the imposing Castel Sant'Angelo (former papal fortress, now a museum) with its fascinating history and rooftop views (~€15). Walk along the scenic Lungotevere riverside promenade — beautiful in the morning light. On Sundays, Via della Conciliazione and surrounding areas are quieter and peaceful.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final Gelato Tour & Souvenir Shopping: Spend your last afternoon doing a self-guided gelato crawl — compare Rome's best gelaterie (Giolitti, Fatamorgana, Gelateria dei Gracchi). Browse for authentic souvenirs in the Prati neighborhood — avoid tourist traps near major monuments and look for local alimentari, ceramic shops, and bookstores.
day_by_day.evening: Departure Preparation & Light Farewell Dinner: Depending on departure time, enjoy a final relaxed dinner near the hotel or in the Prati area. Pack, review transport to the airport, and savor your last Roman evening.

meals.breakfast: Special Sunday breakfast — try a proper Roman Sunday brunch at a café near Castel Sant'Angelo with fresh pastries and cappuccino (~€8–12)
meals.lunch: Light lunch near Prati — a panino from a local forno (bakery) or pizza al taglio (~€6–10)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Osteria dell'Angelo in Prati — beloved local spot with fixed-price Roman menu, excellent value (~€22–28 per person including wine)

day_by_day.notes: Sunday in Rome has a different, slower rhythm — many shops close but churches and museums are open. Check your return flight time and plan airport transfer accordingly: allow 2.5–3 hours before departure for the Leonardo Express journey and check-in. Castel Sant'Angelo is less crowded on Sunday mornings. Keep some euros for tips, last-minute gelato, and transit. Arrivederci Roma!

day_by_day.afternoon: After the Vatican, cross into St. Peter's Basilica for a self-guided exploration of Michelangelo's Pietà and Bernini's magnificent baldachin. Optionally ascend to the dome for panoramic views over Rome. Then transfer to the elegant Prati neighborhood nearby for a relaxed afternoon espresso and gelato at a premium café.
day_by_day.evening: Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk — As the sun sets, join an exclusive small-group or private evening tour through the cobblestone streets of Trastevere. Sample supplì (fried rice balls), Roman-style artichokes, aged pecorino, and local Castelli Romani wines at carefully selected trattorias and wine bars.

meals.breakfast: Lavish buffet breakfast at the resort — fresh pastries, eggs, cured meats, seasonal fruit, and barista coffee
meals.lunch: Ristorante Il Sorpasso (Prati) — upscale Roman tavern with antipasti platters, fresh pasta, and natural wines
meals.dinner: Included in the Trastevere Food & Wine Evening Walk with multiple tastings; supplement with a final glass of wine at Freni e Frizioni rooftop bar

day_by_day.notes: Book Vatican private early-access tour well in advance — availability is extremely limited. Wear comfortable walking shoes. The Vatican Museums and Trastevere are both accessible from central Rome via private car or taxi. Dress modestly for St. Peter's Basilica (shoulders and knees covered).

day_by_day.morning: Campo de' Fiori Market & Cooking Class — Begin the morning at the vibrant Campo de' Fiori market, guided by a professional chef who will help you select the finest seasonal ingredients: heirloom tomatoes, fresh herbs, local cheeses, and prime cuts. Transfer to a private culinary studio nearby for a hands-on cooking class preparing a full Roman menu — antipasto, fresh pasta (cacio e pepe or carbonara), and a traditional dessert.
day_by_day.afternoon: After enjoying the lunch you've cooked, take a leisurely walk through the historic center. Explore the nearby Piazza Navona with its stunning Bernini fountains, then wander to the Pantheon for a private guided visit inside this perfectly preserved ancient marvel. Stop for a premium gelato at Giolitti or Della Palma.
day_by_day.evening: Dress for a sophisticated evening out. Enjoy aperitivo hour at a rooftop bar overlooking the Roman skyline — Hotel Minerva's rooftop or Terrazza Borromini are excellent choices. Follow with dinner at a celebrated restaurant in the historic center.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast service at the resort — freshly squeezed juices, croissants, yogurt parfait, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: The meal prepared during the cooking class, enjoyed with local wine in the culinary studio
meals.dinner: Ristorante Settimio all'Arancio or La Pergola (3 Michelin stars, Rome's pinnacle fine dining) — reserve months in advance; expect a multi-course tasting menu with wine pairing (€300+ per person at La Pergola)

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class typically runs 10:00–14:00. Confirm class language (English) and dietary restrictions in advance. La Pergola requires formal attire and advance reservation. Consider hiring a private driver for the full day for seamless transfers between locations.

day_by_day.morning: Borghese Gallery Art Experience — Secure a private or small-group guided visit to the Villa Borghese's intimate baroque masterpiece gallery. Admire Bernini's awe-inspiring sculptures (Apollo and Daphne, The Rape of Proserpina) and Caravaggio's dramatically lit canvases up close. Entry is strictly timed and limited, making this one of Rome's most exclusive art experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the gallery, stroll through the magnificent Villa Borghese gardens — Rome's Central Park — at a leisurely pace. Rent a rowboat on the lake or simply relax on a bench surrounded by umbrella pines. In the late afternoon, transfer to the Spanish Steps area and explore the luxury boutiques along Via Condotti (Valentino, Bulgari, Fendi) for premium shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a pre-dinner Negroni at Ciampini café near the Spanish Steps, a Roman institution with terrace seating. Proceed to dinner at a celebrated restaurant in the Tridente neighborhood, focusing on creative contemporary Roman cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Caffè Greco on Via Condotti — Rome's oldest café (est. 1760), beloved by Keats, Goethe, and Byron; enjoy cappuccino and cornetti in gilded surroundings
meals.lunch: Casino Valadier inside Villa Borghese gardens — elegant restaurant with panoramic terrace views over Rome; seasonal Roman cuisine
meals.dinner: Imàgo at Hotel Hassler (rooftop, panoramic views of Rome) — refined contemporary Italian cuisine with an extraordinary wine list (approx. €180–€250 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Borghese Gallery tickets must be booked weeks or months in advance — maximum 360 visitors per 2-hour slot. A private guide enhances the experience enormously. The gallery is a short walk or taxi from the resort area. Combine the afternoon shopping with a visit to Bulgari's flagship for a complimentary jewelry viewing experience.

day_by_day.morning: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Sunrise/Morning Tour — Arrange a private guided tour of the ancient heart of the Roman Empire during the cool golden morning hours before crowds arrive. Walk the sacred Via Sacra, explore the ruins of imperial palaces on Palatine Hill, and stand in the Forum where Julius Caesar once spoke. Your expert archaeologist guide will bring 2,000 years of history vividly to life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Colosseum with your private guide — access the arena floor and underground hypogeum (special access ticket required) for an unparalleled behind-the-scenes perspective. Afterward, transfer to the Testaccio neighborhood — Rome's original culinary district — for a private food tour of its covered market and artisan producers.
day_by_day.evening: Palatine Hill & Roman Forum Sunset Tour (optional second visit or alternative) — If you wish to experience the Forum at golden hour as well, return for the sunset session when the light turns the ancient stones amber and the crowds have thinned. Otherwise, enjoy a relaxed evening at the resort spa followed by dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full Italian spread with eggs, pastries, fresh fruit, cold cuts, and premium coffee
meals.lunch: Flavio al Velavevodetto (Testaccio) — legendary Roman trattoria built into the ancient Monte Testaccio; try the coda alla vaccinara and rigatoni con pajata
meals.dinner: Aroma Restaurant at Palazzo Manfredi — possibly Rome's most dramatic dining location with direct Colosseum views; contemporary Roman cuisine (approx. €150–€200 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Colosseum underground/arena floor access well in advance — these special tickets sell out fast. Morning is the best time for Palatine Hill to avoid midday heat (June temperatures can reach 30°C+). Bring water and sun protection. The Testaccio market closes early afternoon, so time the food tour for late morning.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive private art studio visit and contemporary Rome experience — Arrange through the concierge a private visit to a Roman artist's atelier or a behind-the-scenes tour of a lesser-known baroque church with extraordinary art (San Luigi dei Francesi for Caravaggio's St. Matthew cycle, or Santa Maria della Vittoria for Bernini's Ecstasy of Saint Teresa). Follow with a private tour of Palazzo Doria Pamphilj — a hidden gem housing Velázquez's portrait of Pope Innocent X.
day_by_day.afternoon: Indulge in a full luxury spa afternoon at the resort or at a premium day spa in Rome (Kami Spa or the spa at Waldorf Astoria Rome). Book a signature treatment such as a Roman thermal ritual, hot stone massage, or a couple's treatment. Return refreshed for the evening.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell-style premium dinner experience — book a private chef's table experience at one of Rome's top restaurants, or arrange an exclusive private dinner in a historic location (some agencies offer candlelit dinners inside ancient ruins or private palazzo gardens). End the evening with a nightcap at the resort bar overlooking the waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast in your beachfront suite — strawberries, smoked salmon, pastries, and Franciacorta sparkling wine delivered by room service
meals.lunch: Light spa lunch — fresh salads, grilled fish, cold-pressed juices, and herbal teas at the resort pool or spa café
meals.dinner: Chef's table at Metamorfosi (1 Michelin star) or a private palazzo dinner arranged by a luxury concierge service — expect a bespoke multi-course menu (€200–€400+ per person)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday evenings in Rome are lively — book all dinner reservations well in advance. The private palazzo dinner experience should be arranged through a premium concierge service such as Quintessentially or the hotel's own luxury concierge at least 2–3 weeks ahead. The spa afternoon is a perfect recovery day mid-trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Rome — Begin with a slow, indulgent breakfast at the resort. Take one last walk along the beachfront or through a nearby piazza to soak in the Roman atmosphere. Visit a nearby artisan shop or gallery to purchase a meaningful souvenir — a piece of local ceramics, a signed art print, or a bottle of premium Lazio wine to take home.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure time, arrange a final premium experience: a private boat excursion along the Tiber River (if available), a return visit to a favorite neighborhood, or a relaxed afternoon in a rooftop terrace café. Begin packing and prepare for checkout. Private chauffeur transfer to the airport arranged by the concierge.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — ensure all luggage is handled by the hotel's porter service. The private chauffeur will transfer you to the airport in comfort. Enjoy a final espresso at the airport's premium lounge before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Grand final breakfast at the resort — the full spread, enjoyed slowly with no rush; order anything from the à la carte menu as a farewell treat
meals.lunch: Ristorante Pierluigi (Piazza de Ricci) — beloved Roman institution with outdoor terrace; fresh seafood, house-made pasta, and excellent local wines for a memorable final Roman lunch
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight meal (arrange premium in-flight catering if available on your return flight)

day_by_day.notes: Check-out time is typically 12:00 — request a late check-out (14:00 or later) through the concierge to allow a relaxed final morning without rushing. Confirm private transfer timing based on your flight departure. Allow at least 3 hours before an international departure. Tip the concierge and key staff who made the week exceptional — this is customary for luxury stays.
